text:
**False.**

The claim is a longstanding myth. Astronauts (including those on the ISS and Apollo missions) and space agencies such as NASA have repeatedly stated that the Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from low Earth orbit or beyond. It is too narrow (typically a few meters wide), follows terrain that camouflages it, and lacks sufficient contrast with the surrounding landscape under normal viewing conditions. Photographs that appear to show it usually rely on magnification, image processing, or ideal lighting/angles not representative of unaided human eyesight.

Nuance: “Space” is imprecise (LEO vs. higher orbits differ), and rare reports exist of glimpsing linear features under exceptional conditions, but these do not overturn the established consensus that the structure is not naked-eye visible. The fuller misconception—that it is the only man-made object visible from the Moon—is likewise false.
